memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Psoriasis, chronic plaque type.
Patient reports erythematous, scaly plaques on elbows, knees, and scalp for 6 months, associated with mild itching. On examination, well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale are present over extensor surfaces; scalp shows diffuse scaling. No joint pain or nail changes. Smoking status: never.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
clobetasol 0.05% cream apply BD to affected areas
calcipotriol ointment apply OD to affected areas
methotrexate 7.5 mg take orally once weekly
folic acid 5 mg take orally daily

Psoriasis, chronic plaque type.
Patient notes reduced scaling on elbows and knees after 2 months of topical steroids, but persistent scalp itch. Examination shows mild erythema with less scale on elbows/knees; scalp still exhibits thick scale. No new joint symptoms. Smoking status: never.

Psoriasis, chronic plaque type.
Patient reports worsening of scalp plaques with increased itch and mild hair thinning; elbows/knees stable. Examination reveals thick silvery scale over scalp with underlying erythema; extensor lesions show mild erythema, minimal scale. No arthritis. Smoking status: never.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been using the clobetasol on my scalp twice a day and the methotrexate weekly. The scalp is less itchy and the scaling has improved a lot. I still apply the calcipotriol on my body as before. No side effects noticed.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Psoriasis, chronic plaque type.
Patient states scalp itch markedly decreased, scaling reduced; elbows/knees remain clear. Examination shows faint pink patches on scalp with minimal scale; no plaques on extensor surfaces. Liver enzymes stable. Smoking status: never.
